title: feat(daemon): COPILOT is a recognized worker.type
description:
Slice 1 of task-59e1d150 (GitHub Copilot CLI as a fifth agent provider; that row is the closing integration row). No dependency: it can land first.

OBJECTIVE. A seat whose wrapper launched GitHub Copilot CLI registers as worker.type COPILOT. The wrappers export MOE_WORKER_TYPE=COPILOT (task-ab323f85), and moe-proxy already forwards that value verbatim as workerType on claim_next_task and join_team. But normalizeWorkerType in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/joinTeam.ts maps anything outside CLAUDE, CODEX, GEMINI and GROK to CLAUDE.

DELIVERABLE:
- 'COPILOT' in WorkerType (packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts), in WORKER_TYPES and in WORKER_TYPE_SCHEMA's description (joinTeam.ts; claim_next_task reuses that schema). Record<WorkerType, true> makes tsc enforce the list.
- New cases in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/workerType.test.ts.
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md (join_team and claim_next_task workerType) and docs/SCHEMA.md (WorkerType) name COPILOT.
Additive only: the exact, case-sensitive match and the CLAUDE default for any other value stay.

NOT IN SCOPE: the wrappers (task-ab323f85); moe-proxy's comment listing the types (the docs slice); VS Code's WorkerType type (task-7739d4af); the board UI (JetBrains reads worker.type as a free string, MoeJson.kt:732).

VERIFICATION (global rail: never npm ci/build/test in the live checkout): in a git-archive snapshot outside the repo, cd packages/moe-daemon && npm ci && npm run build && npx vitest run src/tools/workerType.test.ts.
definitionOfDone: moe.join_team and moe.claim_next_task with workerType 'COPILOT' record worker.type COPILOT, and an existing CLAUDE record refreshes to COPILOT, proven by new cases in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/workerType.test.ts
workerType 'copilot', 'Copilot' and ' COPILOT ' still record CLAUDE, proven by the same file
WorkerType in packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts and WORKER_TYPES and WORKER_TYPE_SCHEMA's description in joinTeam.ts include COPILOT, and npm run build passes in the snapshot
docs/MCP_SERVER.md (join_team, claim_next_task) and docs/SCHEMA.md (WorkerType) list COPILOT among the worker types
In a git-archive snapshot outside the live checkout, cd packages/moe-daemon && npm ci && npm run build && npx vitest run src/tools/workerType.test.ts exits 0

implementationPlan.description:
Write the tests first, in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/workerType.test.ts. Edit with your own Edit tool: no shell writes, no subagent edits. Reuse the existing helpers (seed, seat, join, claim, onDisk, diskFile, type). Add no new file and no new helper.
(a) Line 14, header comment: change (CLAUDE/CODEX/GEMINI/GROK) to (CLAUDE/CODEX/GEMINI/GROK/COPILOT).
(b) Line 18: `const TYPES: WorkerType[] = ['CLAUDE', 'CODEX', 'GEMINI', 'GROK', 'COPILOT'];`. This one change adds the COPILOT rows of 'registers a new seat reporting %s, in memory and on disk' for join_team (:54) and claim_next_task (:191). It also runs COPILOT through the list_workers round-trip (:414) via both tools.
(c) Both 'declares an optional workerType property' cases (:48 and :185): cast inputSchema as `{ properties: Record<string, { description: string }>; required: string[] }` and add `for (const t of TYPES) expect(schema.properties.workerType.description).toContain(t);`. The shared WORKER_TYPE_SCHEMA must name every recognized type (DoD 3).
(d) Add the same three rows to two tables: the join_team CLAUDE-default table (:61-73, after its 'padded' row) and the claim_next_task CLAUDE-default table (:198-203, after its 'lowercase' row): `['lowercase copilot', { workerType: 'copilot' }], ['capitalised copilot', { workerType: 'Copilot' }], ['padded copilot', { workerType: ' COPILOT ' }],`. This is DoD 2: these values still record CLAUDE. The join_team table also checks the file on disk.
(e) A new join_team case directly before 'leaves an existing seat byte-identical when a rejoin omits workerType' (:94):
  it('refreshes an existing CLAUDE seat to COPILOT on rejoin and changes nothing else', async () => { const before = await seed('worker-claude', 'CLAUDE'); await join('worker-claude', { workerType: 'COPILOT' }); expect(h.state.getWorker('worker-claude')).toEqual({ ...before, type: 'COPILOT' }); expect(onDisk('worker-claude')).toEqual({ ...before, type: 'COPILOT' }); });
(f) A new claim_next_task case directly before 'refreshes the type on an explicit resume and on alreadyAssigned, leaving the attempt alone' (:216):
  it('refreshes an existing CLAUDE seat to COPILOT on a claim, in memory and on disk', async () => { await seat('worker-seat', 'CLAUDE'); expect((await claim('worker-seat', { workerType: 'COPILOT' })).hasNext).toBe(true); expect(h.state.getTask('task-1')?.assignedWorkerId).toBe('worker-seat'); expect(type('worker-seat')).toBe('COPILOT'); expect(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(diskFile('worker-seat'), 'utf-8')).type).toBe('COPILOT'); });
Do not remove or weaken any existing case. Architect's measurement in a scratch snapshot at 9c2129d4, with only this step applied: 7 failed | 60 passed (67). The 7 failures are the two COPILOT new-seat rows, (e), (f), both 'declares' cases and the list_workers round-trip. The three copilot/Copilot/' COPILOT ' rows already pass at base and must stay green, because they fail a trim or upper-case normalization. You do not need to run this RED state; the single gate run is step 4.

Implement in two files, with your own Edit tool:
- packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts:28 becomes `export type WorkerType = 'CLAUDE' | 'CODEX' | 'GEMINI' | 'GROK' | 'COPILOT';`.
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/joinTeam.ts:9 becomes `const WORKER_TYPES: Record<WorkerType, true> = { CLAUDE: true, CODEX: true, GEMINI: true, GROK: true, COPILOT: true };`. Because it is a Record<WorkerType, true>, tsc rejects a union member without its key, and the reverse.
- joinTeam.ts:44, the first sentence of WORKER_TYPE_SCHEMA.description, becomes `'The seat\'s CLI: CLAUDE, CODEX, GEMINI, GROK or COPILOT (exact, case-sensitive). Any other value is recorded as CLAUDE. ' +`. The second sentence stays. claimNextTask.ts:404 reuses this same object, so claim_next_task needs no edit.
Change nothing else:
- normalizeWorkerType keeps its exact Object.hasOwn match and its CLAUDE default.
- Add no trim, no case folding and no enum on the input schema. An unknown value is still recorded as CLAUDE and never refused.
Error handling: this change adds no error-handling path and removes none. normalizeWorkerType cannot throw. refreshWorkerType still logs and swallows a failed type write, so the join or claim still answers; the existing 'logs and swallows a failed type write' cases (:144 and :322) cover this.
No other daemon file needs to change: nothing else in packages/moe-daemon/src branches on a WorkerType value (chatWho.ts and listWorkers.ts:75 only project worker.type).

Update the docs, with your own Edit tool. docs/MCP_SERVER.md has exactly six worker-type enumerations. Add COPILOT last in each:
- :1457 (claim_next_task Parameters): `// the seat's CLI: CLAUDE | CODEX | GEMINI | GROK | COPILOT (see "Reported worker type")`
- :1488 (claim_next_task, Reported worker type): `Names are exact and case-sensitive: `CLAUDE`, `CODEX`, `GEMINI`, `GROK` or `COPILOT`.` (in backticks, as in the existing text)
- :2199 (list_workers response): `// CLAUDE | CODEX | GEMINI | GROK | COPILOT, as claim_next_task / join_team recorded it`
- :2490 (join_team, Reported worker type): `exactly `CLAUDE`, `CODEX`, `GEMINI`, `GROK` or `COPILOT` (case-sensitive) is kept`
- :2497 (join_team Parameters): `// The seat's CLI: CLAUDE | CODEX | GEMINI | GROK | COPILOT (anything else is recorded as CLAUDE)`
- :2802 (chat_who Notes): (`CLAUDE` | `CODEX` | `GEMINI` | `GROK` | `COPILOT`)
The list_workers and chat_who lines are in scope for two reasons. They enumerate the same WorkerType union this task extends, and no sibling slice edits MCP_SERVER.md. Left stale, they would contradict the join_team and claim_next_task lines in the same file.
In docs/SCHEMA.md's WorkerType (:1172-1176), the GROK line loses its semicolon and COPILOT closes the union:
  | 'GROK'      // xAI Grok Build CLI
  | 'COPILOT';  // GitHub Copilot CLI
Leave the NOTE below it (:1177-1183) unchanged. Its sentence that the launchers export CLAUDE, CODEX, GEMINI or GROK stays true until the wrapper slice task-ab323f85 lands, and the closing row task-59e1d150 updates it.
Out of scope; do not touch: docs/CONFIGURATION.md (the closing row), the comment in packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts (the docs slice, task-1c580985), the wrappers, moe-vscode and moe-jetbrains.

Verify once, with a fresh run from the worktree root. Run executionContract.checkRefs[0] verbatim; its shape follows mem:convention-daemon-full-suite-gate-checkref.
What the command does:
1. Checks the docs. Every MCP_SERVER.md line that names GEMINI and GROK must also name COPILOT, and there must be at least six such lines. SCHEMA.md must have the `'COPILOT';  // GitHub Copilot CLI` closer and no `'GROK';` left.
2. Archives HEAD into a mktemp dir outside the repo and overlays the three edited code files.
3. In that snapshot, runs npm ci, npm run build (prebuild included), a tsc typecheck of workerType.test.ts through tt.json (the package tsconfig excludes tests), and npx vitest run src/tools/workerType.test.ts.
Expected: exit 0 and 'Tests  67 passed (67)'. In the architect's dry run the whole command took about 7 s from a clone with uncommitted edits. The run's command, exit code and output tail are your complete_task verification evidence. The build log in the snapshot shows 'generate-init-files: no git history for docs/roles/...' lines; those are expected in a git-archive snapshot (it has no .git) and harmless.
Global rail: never run npm ci, build or test in the live checkout or in the worktree's own packages.
Error handling for a red run:
- 'DOCS STALE': one of the six MCP_SERVER.md lines or the SCHEMA.md union is still stale.
- An 'error TS' line: it names the file and line to fix.
- A failed build: the command prints the last 30 lines of the build log.
- A failed npm ci prints nothing. Rerun `npm ci` without the redirect inside the snapshot dir the command printed ('snapshot <dir>') to see why.
Fix the cause and rerun the whole command. Never edit the command text. Afterwards, remove only your own snapshot dir (the printed path).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Case-insensitive or trimmed matching for COPILOT: rejected. The DoD and the contract that landed with task-0b40957c keep the exact, case-sensitive match and the CLAUDE default.
- An enum on the workerType input schema: rejected. The contract never refuses an unknown value, and MCP_SERVER.md says the schema carries no enum.
- Separate COPILOT-only tests instead of extending TYPES: rejected. Appending to TYPES reuses every it.each(TYPES) row (a new seat via join_team, a new seat via claim_next_task, and the list_workers round-trip) with no new code. Two explicit refresh cases cover the DoD's CLAUDE-to-COPILOT wording.
- Updating SCHEMA.md's launcher NOTE and docs/CONFIGURATION.md now: rejected. The wrappers do not export COPILOT until task-ab323f85 lands, and the closing row task-59e1d150 owns those lines.
- A full daemon-suite gate: rejected. The change is a union member, a record key and a description string. tsc (npm run build) covers every typed consumer, and no code branches on the value. No test pins the description or the doc lines: there are no snapshot files, no budget tests over tool schemas, and the doc-reading tests do not cover these sections. The scoped gate takes about 7 s, far inside the 20-minute budget.
